correctness.rationale: In a complete multipartite graph, a positive vertex is isolated in the positive-induced subgraph exactly when all positive labels lie in its own part; hence totality is equivalent to positive labels occupying at least two parts. A zero in part \(i\) is Roman-dominated exactly when some label two lies outside part \(i\). These two observations give the stated iff criterion. Splitting labelings by whether label two occurs in at least two parts, exactly one part, or no part yields the closed generating polynomial without overlap. Extracting the lowest power gives \(\gamma_{tR}(G)=\min\{N,4,\min_i n_i+2\}\). A fresh exhaustive check on the profiles \((1,1),(2,1),(2,2),(3,2,1),(2,2,2)\) found exact agreement between the literal definition and the part-profile criterion for every labeling; the infinite theorem is the symbolic adjacency argument.
residual_risks: The theorem assumes a connected complete multipartite graph, hence at least two parts.

value.rationale: Total Roman domination is an established graph invariant and complete multipartite graphs are a canonical family. Counting every feasible function by weight is a natural refinement of the minimum parameter and yields that minimum as a corollary while retaining substantially more combinatorial information. The all-part-size symbolic classification gives a reusable enumerator rather than a small finite census.
residual_risks: The proof is elementary because complete multipartite adjacency is especially rigid.
